# Agent console

A person asks an agent a question and watches it work: the transcript of what was said beside a timeline of what was done, with Stop always in reach.

## When to use

- A conversational agent whose answers rest on tool calls and sources a person should be able to check.
- People need to see the agent working, step by step, and stop it part-way without losing what arrived.
- Answers are read, cited and rated, and the session’s token use matters.

## When not to

- The agent has stopped for a person’s decision on one action. Use Agent hand-off.
- Watching a run with no conversation, such as a scheduled job. Use Agent run.
- A single answer in a panel, without a session around it. Use Message.

Read from its imports.

- [Message](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-message--overview.md): Each turn of the Thread, the question and the answer, with copy, retry, rating, and the error when a call fails.
- [Prompt input](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-prompt-input--overview.md): The composer, which becomes Stop while the agent is generating.

- [Sources](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-sources--overview.md): The citations in the answer and the list of what was read.
- [Streaming text](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-streaming-text--overview.md): The answer as it arrives, in Alegreya, with its citations.
- [Token usage](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-token-usage--overview.md): The session’s tokens and cost against the context window.
- [Tool call](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-tool-call--overview.md): The two calls the agent makes, with their arguments and results.

## States

- Empty: Nothing asked yet: what the agent can answer, two suggested questions, and a run panel that says what will appear in it. Story: https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/story/patterns-agent-console--console
- Loading: The agent at work: the plan and the tool calls with their clocks, the answer streaming, the run panel’s steps live, and Stop in the composer. Story: https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/story/patterns-agent-console--working
- Error: A tool call times out: the turn says so once, with the error verbatim and Retry; the run panel marks the step failed and offers Retry run, without a second alert. Story: https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/story/patterns-agent-console--tool-fails
- No permission: No composer to be refused by and no suggestions to press: a callout names who can grant access, and the run panel says runs by others appear there. Story: https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/story/patterns-agent-console--no-permission

## Accessibility

- The transcript is a Thread, a labelled region and not a live one, so a streaming answer is not read aloud token by token; the answer announces its own completion once.
- Stop is the composer’s own button while the agent is generating, so it is where focus already is.
- The answer is not repeated in the run panel, so a screen reader moving through the page hears it once.
- The person’s words are in Archivo and the agent’s in Alegreya, so the two voices can be told apart without colour.

Every AI component, composed into a working console for **Cayuco**, a fictional internal knowledge-and-agent platform. Ask it something (or pick a suggestion): the agent plans, calls two tools, and streams a cited answer, while the run panel on the right shows the same work as a timeline with live clocks and token usage. Press **Stop** mid-answer to see cancellation; the transcript keeps what arrived.

**Decisions.** The transcript is what was said and the run panel is what was done, so the answer is not repeated in the panel. A failed tool call is said once, in the turn, with the error verbatim and Retry; the panel states the failed step without a second alert. Someone who may not ask the agent gets no composer to be refused by: a callout names who can give access.

The screen owns its scripted run rather than importing the story harness from the AI stories, because a pattern may lean only on what the package exports, and exporting a demo harness would ship fixtures to every consumer. The demo content — an in-app help panel rollout — is invented, and there is no model behind this page.
